medial head of gastrocnemius: The larger calf head, arising from the medial condyle of the femur; it tears in 'tennis leg'. The muscle raises the heel and flexes the knee. Tibial nerve.
medial head of triceps brachii: Deep head arising below the radial groove; all three heads insert into the olecranon and extend the elbow.
medial intercondylar tubercle: Medial tubercle of the intercondylar eminence.
medial intermuscular septum of arm: The ulnar nerve pierces this septum to enter the posterior compartment.
medial lip of linea aspera: Medial lip of the linea aspera; vastus medialis and the adductors attach to it.
medial malleolar facet: Comma-shaped surface that articulates with the medial malleolus.
medial malleolus: Lower end of the tibia felt under the skin; the great saphenous vein passes in front of it (emergency venous access).
medial meniscus: C-shaped medial meniscus; attached to the tibial collateral ligament, it is less mobile and tears more often ('unhappy triad').
medial patellar retinaculum: Extension of the vastus medialis aponeurosis; the medial patellofemoral ligament within it prevents lateral dislocation of the patella.
medial process of calcaneal tuberosity: Medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity; abductor hallucis and the plantar aponeurosis arise here.
medial pterygoid muscle: Runs from the pterygoid fossa to the inner surface of the angle of the mandible; with masseter it forms a sling for the mandible and closes the jaw.
medial pterygoid plate: Medial plate of the pterygoid process; the pterygoid hamulus lies at its tip.
medial rectus muscle: The strongest eye muscle, turning the eye inwards (adduction); oculomotor nerve.
medial subtendinous bursa of gastrocnemi: Between the medial head and the capsule; joined with the semimembranosus bursa it can form a Baker's cyst.
medial supracondylar line: Continuation of the linea aspera down to the medial condyle; it ends at the adductor tubercle.
medial surface of arytenoid cartilage: Surface facing the opposite arytenoid; covered by mucosa, it bounds the posterior part of the rima glottidis.
medial surface of fibula: Medial surface of the fibula; the extensor muscles of the anterior compartment arise from it.
medial surface of tibia: Broad anteromedial surface just under the skin; bone grafts and intraosseous access can be taken here.
medial surface of ulna: Medial surface of the ulna; FDP arises from it.
medial talocalcaneal ligament: Binds the medial tubercle of the talus to the sustentaculum tali.
medial tubercle: Medial tubercle of the posterior process; the deltoid ligament attaches to it.
median cricothyroid ligament: Ligament between the thyroid and cricoid cartilages; cricothyrotomy is performed here to open an emergency airway.
median sacral crest: Midline ridge formed by the fused spinous processes.
median thyrohyoid ligament: Thick middle part of the thyrohyoid membrane.
meniscopatellar ligament: Capsular thickening joining the edge of the patella to the menisci.
mental foramen: Foramen below the second premolar; the mental nerve and artery emerge from it.
mental tubercle: Prominence on each side of the mental protuberance.
mentalis muscle: Raises and wrinkles the skin of the chin and pushes the lower lip forwards (pouting).
mesial surface of tooth: Surface of a tooth facing the front (midline) of the dental arch.
metacarpal bones: Five long bones forming the skeleton of the palm; they articulate with the proximal phalanges of the fingers.
metatarsal interosseous ligaments: Interosseous ligaments between adjacent metatarsal bases.
middle cells of ethmoid bone: Air cells forming the ethmoidal bulla; they open into the middle meatus.
middle clinoid process: Small process at the anterolateral corner of the sella turcica; sometimes fused with the anterior clinoid.
middle facet for calcaneus: Middle surface that articulates with the sustentaculum tali.
middle glenohumeral ligament: Limits anterior translation in moderate abduction.
middle layer of thoracolumbar fascia: Layer between erector spinae and quadratus lumborum.
middle phalanx of fifth finger of foot: Middle bone of the little toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.
middle phalanx of fifth finger of hand: Middle bone of the little finger; it lies between the proximal and distal phalanges.
middle phalanx of fourth finger of foot: Middle bone of the 4th toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.
middle phalanx of fourth finger of hand: Middle bone of the ring finger; it lies between the proximal and distal phalanges.
middle phalanx of second finger of foot: Middle bone of the 2nd toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.
middle phalanx of second finger of hand: Middle bone of the index finger; it lies between the proximal and distal phalanges.
middle phalanx of third finger of foot: Middle bone of the 3rd toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.
middle phalanx of third finger of hand: Middle bone of the middle finger; it lies between the proximal and distal phalanges.
middle pharyngeal constrictor: Fan-shaped constrictor arising from the horns of the hyoid bone.
multifidus lumborum muscle: Deep muscle, thickest in the lumbar region, spanning 2–4 segments; it provides segmental stability and wastes in low back pain.
